title: Stepwise upgrade cohorts and safety automation for model/runtime releases
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a cohort-based progressive delivery system and runbook for runtime/model releases that guarantees predictable promotion to LTS channels while minimizing blast radius. This task covers the policy design, telemetry signals, automated gate engine, and rollback choreography integrated with Console and Release Orchestrator.

Scope and deliverables:
- Cohort scheduling: define release cohorts (internal canary, 1% pilot, 5% ramp, 25% ramp, steady-state) and traffic map templates per release type (hotfix vs major).
- Gate engine: implement a configurable gate DSL to express pass/fail rules over multiple signals (p99 latency, error-rate, token-cost delta, quality regressions from smoke prompts).
- Safety automation: circuit-breaker that auto-triggers rollback when composite score exceeds thresholds, with backoff and cooldown windows.
- Feature-flag integration: tie rollouts to feature flags for fast kill-switch and partial routing by customer segment.
- Promotion workflow: automatic promotion policy into LTS if stable for a configurable stability window (default 14 days) and manual approval path for exceptional promotion.
- Observability: Console dashboards and a canary summary API endpoint that surfaces cohort-level diffs, regression alerts, and rollback rationale.
- Release runbook: step-by-step playbook for on-call and SRE including mitigation steps, whitelist overrides, and escalation contacts.

Acceptance criteria:
- New gate DSL supports expression of composite rules and can be evaluated against historical telemetry within 2 minutes of ingestion.
- Canary run returns pass/fail and a human-readable rationale; passing canaries auto-schedule the next cohort unless manual hold is set.
- Auto-rollback happens without human interaction within 60s of meeting failure thresholds for critical signals and logs the event in Console with a revert PR link.
- Integration tests (kitchen/system) that simulate increased error-rate and latency cause rollback in the test environment and generate the expected alerts/annotations.

Non-goals: rollout UI redesign (Console will use existing widgets), long-term evaluation pipelines (handled by Optimize).
